oil_refined_fuel_inflation.title: Oil, refined-fuel scarcity and inflation
oil_refined_fuel_inflation.hypothesis: Physical crude and refined-product disruption can sustain inflation and tighten financial conditions.
counterdrivers: Saudi rerouting and alternative procurement reduce immediate crude-shortage risk.
US product inventories increased and four-week gasoline/distillate demand was below year-earlier levels.

expression.proxy: Brent/WTI, diesel cracks and energy-versus-broad-equity dashboards
expression.limits: No single proxy cleanly separates crude disruption, refinery scarcity and Fed/USD effects.

fundamental_tests: Official physical-flow data show whether Saudi crude exports are restored, rerouted or lost.
Refined-product inventories, throughput and exports establish whether diesel scarcity is normalizing.
catalysts: Federal Reserve decision and guidance on September 16, 2026.
Official Saudi pipeline/restoration and shipping-flow updates.
Weekly EIA inventories and subsequent inflation releases.
paper_risks: Crude and refined products can diverge sharply.
Geopolitical headlines can gap markets outside liquid hours.
Without holdings, costs and option surfaces, no portfolio hedge or P&L can be validated.
decisions: Approve separate crude-disruption and refined-fuel risk buckets rather than one combined oil position.
Define the evidence required for restoration and the maximum event-risk budget before considering activation.
Decide whether existing energy, inflation and USD exposure already duplicates this theme.
coverage: US inflation, Fed, Treasury yields and USD
oil_refined_fuel_inflation.invalidation: Separate crude restoration from refined-fuel normalization; neither is established by rerouting alone.

ai_capex_repricing.title: AI capital spending and semiconductor repricing
ai_capex_repricing.hypothesis: Potential semiconductor underperformance; an investment slowdown is not established.
counterdrivers: ASML's latest verified outlook described strong AI-driven demand.
Political and industry resistance to mandatory development slowdowns weakens the policy-restriction channel.

expression.limits: A dollar-for-dollar pair is not beta neutral; export controls and the hardware cycle are confounders.

catalysts: Official hyperscaler capex revisions or binding AI restrictions; dates remain unverified.
ai_capex_repricing.invalidation: Suspend the bearish spending thesis after two relevant reporting rounds reaffirm or raise comparable capex/revenue plans with sustained AI demand; separately, two SMH/SPY closes at least 3% above the anchor invalidate the current bearish market setup.
paper_risks: No qualifying capex or supplier-guidance cut has occurred.
The proxy embeds semiconductor beta and export-control exposure.
Liquidity, borrowing, hedge ratios and option costs have not been checked.
decisions: Keep the theme exploratory until a qualifying company guidance cut or binding restriction occurs.
Decide whether SMH/SPY is acceptable as a dashboard only or whether a beta-adjusted basket is required.
Map existing technology and growth exposure before assigning any risk.
fundamental_tests: A named hyperscaler cuts comparable annual capex guidance by at least 5%.
ASML, Nvidia or TSMC cuts comparable forward revenue guidance by at least 5% and cites weaker AI demand or cancellations.

japan_normalization.title: Japan monetary normalization and yen repricing
japan_normalization.hypothesis: Potential yen appreciation if BOJ policy exceeds expectations.
counterdrivers: A routine 25bp hike is already substantially anticipated.
Fiscal-funding uncertainty can weaken the yen even as Japanese yields rise.

expression.proxy: FXY with USD/JPY and US-Japan two-year spread cross-checks
expression.limits: FXY is a USD-priced proxy, not a carry portfolio, and fresh comparable yield-spread history remains incomplete.

catalysts: BOJ policy decision and guidance on September 18, 2026.
BOJ Summary of Opinions on October 1, 2026.
japan_normalization.invalidation: Suspend after two scheduled meetings without tightening and removal of the official tightening bias; separately, two FXY closes at least 2% below the anchor invalidate the bullish-yen market setup.
paper_risks: Expected tightening may already be priced.
US rates and the dollar can dominate the yen response.
FXY tracking, liquidity, spreads and carry costs have not been fully documented.
decisions: Predefine what BOJ outcome constitutes a positive surprise beyond a routine 25bp hike.
Choose whether the eventual portfolio expression is spot FX, FXY, options or a rates/FX combination only after costs are verified.
Measure existing Fed, USD and carry exposure before assigning Japan risk.
fundamental_tests: Official BOJ guidance retains a conditional tightening bias.
The BOJ implements at least a 25bp increase above the July 31 1.0% baseline.

china_domestic_demand.title: China household-demand weakness versus industrial resilience
china_domestic_demand.hypothesis: Potential consumer-discretionary underperformance with stimulus-reversal risk.
counterdrivers: Industrial output and high-tech/green activity remain comparatively resilient.
Targeted household support or changing financing channels could improve pricing before reported consumption.

expression.limits: Overlapping holdings and sector weights make the ratio an imperfect household-demand hedge.

catalysts: Next official retail, investment and property releases; exact date remains unverified.
Any funded household-support or material property-support package.
china_domestic_demand.invalidation: Suspend when retail-sales growth reaches at least 3% in two consecutive monthly releases and property-investment growth improves to at least -14.9%; separately, two CHIQ/MCHI closes at least 3% above the anchor invalidate the bearish market setup.
paper_risks: CHIQ is an offshore equity proxy rather than a retail-sales index.
Stimulus headlines can reprice equities before implementation details emerge.
Fund overlap, FX and trading costs have not been modeled.
decisions: Decide whether CHIQ/MCHI overlap is acceptable or a cleaner consumer-versus-industrial basket is required.
Set the policy detail needed for a funded-stimulus reversal trigger.
Map China, emerging-market and global-growth exposure before adding the theme.
fundamental_tests: Latest monthly retail-sales growth is below 1% year over year.
Latest year-to-date fixed-asset investment growth is negative.

europe_defense.title: European defense spending converting into company revenue
europe_defense.hypothesis: Potential European defense outperformance, conditional on delivery and valuation.
counterdrivers: Rheinmetall's cancellation-related guidance cut shows that larger budgets do not guarantee supplier delivery.

expression.limits: Matching European closes and price conventions are required; the EUR listing does not eliminate underlying currency exposure.

catalysts: Parliamentary disposition of Germany's 2027 budget; exact date remains unverified.
Funded contract awards and supplier guidance/cash-flow releases.
europe_defense.invalidation: Reassess if the finalized comparable German ministry budget is below EUR98.73bn. Suspend the equity thesis if two current top-five holdings cut comparable revenue guidance by at least 5% and WDEF/STOXX 600 is at least 5% below baseline for two closes.
paper_risks: Draft budgets and cooperation letters are not enacted appropriations or funded revenue.
Supplier execution, working capital and valuation can overwhelm spending headlines.
WDEF official-close continuity, holdings, spreads and hedging costs require verification.
decisions: Require funded contract conversion and cash-flow evidence before treating budget headlines as revenue.
Verify WDEF holdings, official closes, liquidity and concentration before using it as the portfolio proxy.
Decide the valuation and drawdown limits that would override otherwise supportive spending evidence.
fundamental_tests: Comparable German defense-ministry budget is at least 10% above the prior-year target.
Rheinmetall latest quarterly revenue grows at least 20% year over year.
